subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: For Claude CLI sessions with an OpenClaw auth profile, should the auth epoch treat unchanged credential identity as stable when the local credentials file appears or disappears, and where should that policy live?
rationale: The source-repro is clear, but changing auth-epoch inputs defines the session/auth boundary and can affect when existing sessions survive or reset.

options.title: Profile credential owns identity when present
options.body: Exclude or suppress the local Claude file fingerprint once the selected auth-profile credential exists, keep a bootstrap fallback, and test real identity changes separately.

options.title: Host credential owns Claude CLI
options.body: Adopt a host-owned mode for Claude CLI and separately make local credential presence identity-stable, otherwise the exact file absent/present flip can remain unresolved.

options.title: Keep storage-sensitive invalidation
options.body: Treat any local credential source-presence change as a reset boundary and accept the reported session-continuity cost.

recommendation.title: Profile credential owns identity when present
recommendation.body: Exclude or suppress the local Claude file fingerprint once the selected auth-profile credential exists, keep a bootstrap fallback, and test real identity changes separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the auth-epoch invalidation policy is the original auth-epoch commit plus later related merge activity.
